Actually I need to show you two how to use Eldarica as well, the Horn solver that does *not* come by default you'll need that for more complex cases Great! Looking forward to it. I'll try to go over the links you sent and get back when I'm able to deal with more complex cases <@!430748255807078400> Thanks for the resources! Regarding using Eldarica: If I understand correctly, one would basically need to run the compiler with `settings.modelChecker.solvers=smtlib2` and provide a `smtSolver` callback that executes Eldarica (this callback will probably look very similar to the default one provided here https://github.com/ethereum/solc-js/blob/master/smtsolver.js). Would this be the way to do it? exactly! if you use this solc-js branch: https://github.com/ethereum/solc-js/tree/smt_proper_tests https://gist.github.com/leonardoalt/0348b759856b7ce38fd8a98fa2ebff04 and run this script with node inside the solc-js dir with `a.sol` also in that dir and have `eld` in your PATH it should do the whole thing using Eldarica which you can get here: https://github.com/uuverifiers/eldarica/ (i usually just download the latest nightly) the JSON input spec is here: https://docs.soliditylang.org/en/v0.8.11/using-the-compiler.html#compiler-input-and-output-json-description from that point you can also just change the JSON input to bigger contracts, change model checker options, eldarica options, etc etc that solc-js branch is a bit of a mess but makes it a lot easier to run Eldarica hopefully it will get into master soon Awesome, thank you for the detailed information! definitely gonna try this out no worries, lmk if you run into any trouble

excerpts.author: juan_runtime
excerpts.content: <@!430748255807078400> Hi! This is Juan, from RV as well. Thanks for sharing this material! I'll be paying with SMTChecker and try to apply it to some real use cases. Nice presentation you gave yesterday!

excerpts.author: leonardoalt
excerpts.content: Nice, thanks! Actually I need to show you two how to use Eldarica as well, the Horn solver that does *not* come by default

excerpts.author: leonardoalt
excerpts.content: you'll need that for more complex cases

excerpts.author: juan_runtime
excerpts.content: Great! Looking forward to it. I'll try to go over the links you sent and get back when I'm able to deal with more complex cases

excerpts.author: _dawit
excerpts.content: <@!430748255807078400> Thanks for the resources! Regarding using Eldarica: If I understand correctly, one would basically need to run the compiler with `settings.modelChecker.solvers=smtlib2` and provide a `smtSolver` callback that executes Eldarica (this callback will probably look very similar to the default one provided here https://github.com/ethereum/solc-js/blob/master/smtsolver.js). Would this be the way to do it?

excerpts.author: leonardoalt
excerpts.content: exactly!

excerpts.author: leonardoalt
excerpts.content: if you use this solc-js branch: https://github.com/ethereum/solc-js/tree/smt_proper_tests

excerpts.author: leonardoalt
excerpts.content:
https://gist.github.com/leonardoalt/0348b759856b7ce38fd8a98fa2ebff04
and run this script with node inside the solc-js dir

excerpts.author: leonardoalt
excerpts.content: with `a.sol` also in that dir

excerpts.author: leonardoalt
excerpts.content: and have `eld` in your PATH

excerpts.author: leonardoalt
excerpts.content: it should do the whole thing using Eldarica

excerpts.author: leonardoalt
excerpts.content:
which you can get here: https://github.com/uuverifiers/eldarica/
(i usually just download the latest nightly)

excerpts.author: leonardoalt
excerpts.content:
the JSON input spec is here:
https://docs.soliditylang.org/en/v0.8.11/using-the-compiler.html#compiler-input-and-output-json-description

excerpts.author: leonardoalt
excerpts.content: from that point you can also just change the JSON input to bigger contracts, change model checker options, eldarica options, etc etc

excerpts.author: leonardoalt
excerpts.content: that solc-js branch is a bit of a mess but makes it a lot easier to run Eldarica

excerpts.author: leonardoalt
excerpts.content: hopefully it will get into master soon

excerpts.author: _dawit
excerpts.content: Awesome, thank you for the detailed information! definitely gonna try this out

excerpts.author: leonardoalt
excerpts.content: no worries, lmk if you run into any trouble
